exogenous gonadotrophic stimulation of xenografted porcine ovarian tissue can improve the meiotic and embryonic competence of oocytes within primordial follicles.
gonadotrophintreatments of the host mice accelerated follicular growth and development in xenografts and improved the meiotic and development abilities of the oocyte in primordial follicles.

the possibility of obtaining pig blastocysts from primordial follicles.
the development of a novel technology to produce porcine blastocysts by using primordial follicles as the starting material, which could lead to the production of porcine clones.
the development of a novel technology for the production of porcine embryos from primordial follicles.

the present results indicate that the meiotic competence of oocytes within the xenografted porcine primordials was improved by exogenous gonadotropin treatments of host mice.

exogenous gonadotropins, not mouse FSH, stimulate the growing follicles which have developed from the primodial follicles in the grafts and that these effects improved the meiotic and development abilities of oocytes to some extent, although the effects were incomplete.

the oocytes in porine primordial follicules can be rescued by the gonadotropin treatments.
the oocyte competence in the xenografted porcine primodial follicles was improved by exogenous gonadotropin treatment of the host mice.
the meiotic competence of oocytes from porcine primodial follicles can be enhanced by gonadotrophine treatment of the recipient mice, although the developmental potential is not yet fully restored.

the xenografted porcine primordium follicle system can be a useful model for studying the mechanisms of follicle development and oocyte maturation, and may be applicable to the production of transgenic pigs.
